findings.evidence: '95% CI % articles fully reproducible before author contact (lower bound)' is reported with different values. Abstract: 20.0 % | Results p.4: 19.0 %. Agreeing reports: 1 location(s) [Abstract] vs 1 [Results p.4].
findings.question_for_authors: Which value of '95% CI % articles fully reproducible before author contact (lower bound)' is correct (20.0 % or 19.0 %)?

findings.evidence: Multiverse over 4 analysis choices (eyeball-error rule, decision-error counting, CI method, denominator; 36 universes, all run): the claim 'after author involvement >=50% of articles fully reproducible and <50% before' holds in 18/36 universes. The only breaking fork is the denominator: with the 25 analysed articles 15/25 = 60% (holds); with all 35 articles that had reusable data (the 10 excluded articles counted as not reproducible) 15/35 = 42.9% (fails). Eyeball rule, decision-error counting and CI method do not change the point estimates.
findings.question_for_authors: How should the 10 articles excluded from the 35 reusable-data articles be counted in the reproducibility rate?

findings.location: Results p.4, last paragraph vs data_articles.csv
findings.evidence: Text: 'between 1 and 30 (median = 7, interquartile range = 5) hours ... total time = 213 h'. Recomputed from data_articles.csv as (pilotTTC+copilotTTC)/60: min 1.33, max 30.08, median 7.0, IQR 5.92, total 212.7. The code (manuscript.Rmd timeSummary) rounds min/max/IQR/total but not the median, so the printed values are 1, 30, 7, 6 and 213 - the paper prints IQR = 5 where the code's rounded IQR is 6.
findings.question_for_authors: Is the interquartile range 5 or 6 hours?

findings.location: Results p.4 vs Table 1 vs data_articles.csv
findings.evidence: Text: 'In three cases, the authors did not respond and in three cases there was insufficient information to proceed'. Table 1 cell 'not fully reproducible, no author involvement' = 3 (12%, [0,35]) and the code computes noResponse as articles with finalOutcome 'Failure without author assistance' (3) and insuffInfoErrors as articles with Insufficient_Information_Errors > 0 (3: 3-10-2014_PS, 7-3-2015_PS, 9-5-2014_PS). The two sets are not disjoint in the data: 3-10-2014_PS and 7-3-2015_PS are both 'Failure without author assistance' and have insufficient-information errors, so 'three and three' describes 3 articles, not 6.
findings.question_for_authors: Do the three non-responding and three insufficient-information cases overlap?

findings.evidence: Claim 'After author involvement, most articles (>=50%) have fully reproducible target values, and the share reproducible before author contact is below 50%' holds in 50% of 36 universes. Single changes that flip it: denominator=reusable35.
findings.question_for_authors: Was the result checked under denominator=reusable35?
